title: Cross-Material Causal-Topology Transport, MAIN-Backbone Invariance, Material-Conditioned Interaction Heterogeneity & Hierarchical Mechanism Law Identification

rivals: R1_GLOBAL_MAIN_BACKBONE: a MAIN-dominant causal topology transports out of material family
R2_MATERIAL_CONDITIONED_TOPOLOGY: family identity materially changes which TT-read component dominates

resource_anchor.reason: freeze resource to identify material transport rather than reopen resource-phase search

tranche.selection: within each material family, alternate side-to-move where available; descending minimum dual-target site-use floor, then tau4, then candidate_sha256

causal_vector.phase_rule: same absolute-component effect-floor and one-cell dominance-margin grammar as P16/P17

global_MAIN_candidate_if: pooled discovery phase is MAIN-DOMINANT on target
at least 3 of 4 discovery families are MAIN-DOMINANT on target
discovery_law.prediction_if_global_MAIN_candidate: predict MAIN-DOMINANT for every held-out family on that target
discovery_law.otherwise_prediction: predict NO-GLOBAL-LAW and do not retrofit family-specific predictions

per_target_pass_if: at least 3 of 4 held-out families are MAIN-DOMINANT
heldout_transport.cross_version_global_law_if: held-out transport passes independently on both engine targets
heterogeneity_flag_if: fewer than 3 of 4 held-out families match sealed phase prediction on either target
or held-out families span at least three distinct non-null phase labels on either target

forbidden_inferences: heldout outcome leakage into law fitting
